cases.name: repeatable-regression-loop
cases.description: The diagnosis makes an R failure minimal and turns the confirmed bug into a regression test.
cases.prompt: An R function fails only for one malformed input in a production report. Describe how to diagnose it and what to do after identifying the root cause.
traps: The model proposes a speculative patch without first making the failure repeatable.
The model stops after the fix without adding a regression test or checking nearby behavior.

assertions.text: Creates a minimal reproducible example while preserving useful non-failing contrasts.
Uses concrete hypotheses and controlled experiments to locate the violated assumption.
Adds a focused regression test and checks behavior that must remain valid.

cases.name: traceback-tool-choice
cases.description: The answer selects an appropriate stack and interactive tool for the failure mode.
cases.prompt: An rlang error occurs while evaluating a lazy argument several calls below the public function. Which tools should you use first, and how should you interpret them?
traps: The model recommends only traceback() and ignores the call tree.
The model leaves global error or warning options enabled after debugging.

assertions.text: Uses rlang::with_abort() and rlang::last_trace() for the lazy-evaluation call tree.
Explains how to use traceback() as a base-R alternative and how to read the stack.
Keeps temporary debugging options and instrumentation scoped to the investigation.

cases.name: batch-only-failure
cases.description: The diagnosis accounts for non-interactive state and preserves evidence for later inspection.
cases.prompt: An R Markdown job fails on CI but succeeds interactively. Give a focused debugging plan that preserves the batch call frames and checks the likely environment differences.
traps: The model assumes the interactive session is authoritative.
The model recommends connecting to production or dumping sensitive inputs into logs.

assertions.text: Reproduces through an explicit render or fresh process rather than relying on IDE knitting state.
Uses dump.frames() or a focused trace for non-interactive evidence.
Compares global objects, attached packages, working directory, PATH, R_LIBS, inputs, locale, and versions without leaking secrets.
